how.title: How a call becomes your order
how.lede: Three steps in between. None of them are yours.
how.s1.title: The team calls it
how.s1.body: A signal team watches gold and posts direction, entry, stop and targets to the group when they see something. The capture machine reads their format and pulls the numbers out — you never have to read or remember them.
how.s2.title: Everyone gets it in seconds
how.s2.body: Parsed signals go straight to the cloud and reach every member at the same moment — nobody gets it first. The same signal never fires twice, and stale ones are never backfilled.
how.s3.title: Your MT5 places the order
how.s3.body: The app on your computer takes the signal and sends the order to your own broker account, at the size and strategy you set. Your money never leaves your account, not once.
feat.title: Hands off, but the risk is yours to set
feat.lede: Same call, and one member trades 0.01 lots while another trades 0.5. Everything that's yours to decide, we hand to you.
feat.martingale.title: You decide how many steps
feat.martingale.body: Multiplier, how many steps, the size at each one — all yours. Sources count their steps separately, so a losing run on one never drags the other down. Reset to step one whenever you want.
feat.partial.title: Bank some, let the rest run free
feat.partial.body: When a call carries several targets, close in portions. Or move the stop to entry the moment the first target fills, and the rest can run without risk. Pick one per source.
feat.sources.title: Follow this one, pause that one
feat.sources.body: Follow this one, pause that one. Martingale here, flat sizing there. Different lot sizes for each. A paused source leaves the screen, and the reports stop counting it.
feat.risk.title: It stops itself at your daily line
feat.risk.body: Set an amount or a percentage. Hit it and nothing new opens for the rest of the day. Orders left unfilled too long get pulled, and the MT5 order goes with them.
feat.schedule.title: Set the hours once
feat.schedule.body: Set a start time and a stop time. Outside market hours the clock pauses — leaving the app open doesn't burn your plan time.
feat.report.title: Know exactly what this month made
feat.report.body: Equity curve, win rate, profit factor — today, this week, this month, broken out by source. Tag your own EAs and they show up in the same report.

faq.title: Ask first
faq.q1: Do you ever touch my money?
faq.a1: No. Your funds stay in the broker account you opened yourself. We never hold them, never move them, and never need your broker password. The system does one thing: it writes an order instruction into the MT5 folder on your computer, and the EA on your chart sends it. Close the app and it stops.
faq.q2: Do I have to leave my computer on?
faq.a2: Your computer and MT5 need to be running so there's something to place the order when a call comes in — but you don't have to sit there. Plan time only counts down while the app is actually running, and pauses outside market hours.
faq.a3: Any broker with MetaTrader 5, which is probably the one you already use. Orders are written into your local MT5 folder and executed by the EA on your chart — nothing routes through a third-party account.
faq.a4: Yes. It scales up after every loss, and if price keeps running against you the drawdown grows fast. That's why you set the maximum number of steps, the size at each one, and a daily loss limit that stops everything. Those are controls, not guarantees. Only risk money you can afford to lose entirely.
faq.a5: By how long the app actually runs, not by calendar days. It doesn't count while the app is off, and it pauses outside market hours. Choose yearly to use all 12 months while paying for only 9.
cta.title: You can start today
cta.lede: Message us for the installer and your account, attach the EA, sign in. After that you just leave it running and it does the work.

features.title: Six things, all yours to set
features.lede: The call gives you direction and price. How much to trade, whether to scale, when to stop — all decided on your machine.
f1.title: You decide how many steps
f1.body: Set the multiplier, the maximum number of steps, and the lot size at each step individually. Every signal source counts its own ladder, so one losing streak never drags another source down. Reset to step one by hand at any time.
f1.p1: Step sizes from a multiplier, or written out step by step
f1.p2: Ladders are fully isolated between sources
f1.p3: Ladder state survives a restart — it does not start over
f2.title: Bank some, let the rest run free
f2.body: When a signal carries several take-profit levels you can close in proportional tranches, or switch to moving the stop to entry as soon as the first target prints, leaving the rest to run at zero risk. Chosen per source.
f2.p2: Break-even mode: the stop moves once TP1 fills
f2.p3: Each source picks its own mode
f3.title: Follow this one, pause that one
f3.body: Every signal source is its own set of settings: follow or ignore, martingale or flat sizing, and how much. Disabled sources take up no screen space and are excluded from the statistics.
f3.p1: Follow toggle, sizing mode and lot size, per source
f3.p2: Disabled sources drop out of the layout and the stats
f3.p3: Sources not yet live can be configured in advance
f4.title: It stops itself at your daily line
f4.body: Set the most you are willing to lose in a day, as an amount or a share of capital. Crossing it stops trading for the rest of the day. Pending orders that sit unfilled past your timeout are cancelled, and MT5 is told to delete the order.
f4.p1: Daily loss cap as an amount or a percentage
f4.p2: Unfilled orders auto-cancel — three hours by default
f4.p3: Cancellation is pushed to MT5; no ghost orders left behind
f5.title: Set the hours once

f5.p3: Starts with the machine and connects after sign-in

faqp.metaTitle: FAQ & Support | AI Gold Copy Trading
faqp.metaDesc: How copying works, the risks, plan billing, installation, and how to reach us.
faqp.title: Ask first
faqp.lede: Everything we get asked, written down. Anything else, just message us.
faqp.a6: They come from independent third-party providers who post gold entry and exit levels in their own groups. We capture them, parse them into structured order instructions, and send those to your MT5. We do not generate the signals and are not responsible for their accuracy.
faqp.q7: How long from the call to the fill?
faqp.a7: The central capture machine parses the signal and pushes it to the cloud hub immediately; the client polls once a second. End-to-end latency is usually a few seconds. The actual fill also depends on your network, your broker's servers and the liquidity at that moment.
faqp.q8: Can I follow only one source?
faqp.a8: Yes. Every source is its own set of settings — follow or ignore, martingale or flat, and how much. A disabled source disappears from the layout and is excluded from the statistics.
faqp.a9: No. Every order instruction is generated on your own computer, written into your local MT5 folder, and executed by the EA on your chart. Your funds stay between you and your broker — we never handle them, hold them, or move them.
faqp.q10: Is there a cap on losses?
faqp.a10: There isn't one. You can set a maximum daily loss and the system stops when it's hit, but that's a soft control, not a guarantee — gaps, slippage and extreme moves can all push the real loss past your number. Margin trading can cost you your entire deposit. Only risk what you can afford to lose.
faqp.q11: Can I stop at any time?
faqp.a11: Yes. Press Stop and no new signals are taken. Positions already open are not closed automatically; you decide in MT5 whether to hold or close them.
faqp.a12: Message us on Instagram or LINE to arrange it. Once your account is opened you receive a username and password to sign in with.
faqp.a13: Yes. Contact us to upgrade or downgrade. The change takes effect immediately on the device you are signed in on — no reinstall needed.
faqp.a14: One device online at a time. Signing in on a new machine signs the old one out, so the same signal is never placed twice.
faqp.a15: MetaTrader 5 only. The system relies on MT5's file bridge and its EA to place orders; there is no MT4 equivalent implemented.
faqp.q16: Why does MT5 show as disconnected?
faqp.a16: Usually one of three things: MT5 is closed or not signed in, the EA is not attached to a chart, or Allow algorithmic trading is unticked. The client's status log names the file it cannot read, which normally points straight at the cause.
faqp.q17: Can I run two copy accounts on one machine?
faqp.a17: Yes — start the second one with the --instance flag and its settings and records stay entirely separate. Each MT5 account still maps to exactly one client.
faqp.contactBody: Send us a message with what you are seeing. Include the error text if there is one — it speeds things up considerably.
faqp.contactHours: Response time depends on volume, usually within one business day
